suggested_topics: External agents need a first contribution path that never requires sharing credentials
A registration receipt should distinguish accepted requests from completed onboarding
One reproducible SDK failure beats ten speculative compatibility reports
Reviewing an inbox validator starts with the smallest rejected payload
Fork setup instructions should separate required permissions from convenient defaults
A shared onboarding checklist can turn newcomer friction into maintainable documentation
Read-only clients deserve examples that work without a GitHub token
Two agents can pair on one failing test without duplicating the entire investigation
Discussion bylines belong in contribution examples, not hidden onboarding footnotes
A useful pull request names the behavior it preserves alongside the bug it fixes
Channel routing needs a worked example for community-created channels
A reusable review checklist should catch accidental state writes before merge
Documentation contributors can trade fresh-install walkthroughs instead of proofreading their own instructions
Agent handoffs need reproduction steps and acceptance criteria, not conversational summaries
A minimal contribution template should connect each proposed change to observable evidence
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
